note: The tavern common room on the BARE plate (1536x1024). Canon's hiring hall, so
the crowd is the point: docs/04 §3.5's candidates are the people in this room.
One fire sprite, on the hearth. Everything else lit in here is a 6-10px candle
or a wall sconce, and a 16x24 flame strip would be bigger than the candle it is
supposed to be in, so those are breathing PointLight2Ds with no sprite.
figure_scale 1 (W1-STAGE, STAGE-02): stools are ~22px and tables ~90px on this plate, so
the 1x strips are already nearly plate-native (Q01 rules 1x vs 1.5x). The hearth strip is
cut at 64, the width gen_fire.lua draws it at — 48 made every window straddle two flames
(STAGE-11).
Fourteen figures at the bar, the tables, the stage and the door. Checked with
`python tools/art/preview_scene.py stage_tavern`.
Bubbles (W2-STAGE2, TOWN-26): mugs at the bar and the near table, a note over the figure
on the stage, zzz at the door; three are up at a time (a full room). `speech.speaker` is
a list of bubble-free patrons — the line's hash picks its mouth.
`furniture` (W7-STAGE, UI-07): the plate's table tops, the two long tables with their benches,
and the bar counter with its stools, as [x, y, w, h] in plate pixels — where nobody can STAND.
test_scene_stage asserts no actor mark lies inside one; the speaker at the long table's bench
(792,722) moved to the floor beside it (836,730), and three more marks that sat on a bench edge
moved a few pixels off it. The stage's speech plate is sized for the 1x figures: `speech.size`
is the authored box and the Label takes `size.x - 16`, so 156 is a 140px line — the same wrap
SceneStage.SAY_WRAP_1X gives an in-fight line on a 1x scene, rather than the camp's 182/166.

lines: I have killed a rat. Professionally.
I can start today. I can start now.
My last guild? We don't talk about it.
I own my own sword. Mostly own it.
I read the strategy. Most of it.
Do we still get paid if we run?
